subject: Literature
title: Wole Soyinka: Africa's First Laureate
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Wole Soyinka: Africa's First Laureate.

hook.text: In 1986, Wole Soyinka became the first African writer to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.

buildup.text: His plays, poetry, and essays drew on Yoruba mythology and confronted political tyranny in Nigeria.

discovery.text: Soyinka had been imprisoned for two years during the Nigerian Civil War for attempting to broker peace.

twist.text: He wrote poetry on toilet paper in solitary confinement and smuggled the poems out of prison in his clothes.

climax.text: His Nobel told the world that African literature was not a minor tradition but a force equal to any on Earth.

punchline.text: A man who wrote poems on toilet paper won the Nobel Prize.

quiz.question: How did Soyinka write while imprisoned during the Nigerian Civil War?
options: Guards secretly provided him with notebooks
He wrote poetry on toilet paper and smuggled it out
He dictated his poems to a fellow prisoner
